statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-56392 is an integer overflow in unexpand buffer allocation that multiplies max_column_width by MB_LEN_MAX. That allocation path was introduced after coreutils 9.7 (multibyte expand/unexpand support; first present in 9.11). Debian trixie and this DHI package ship 9.7, which still allocates with ximalloc(max_column_width) and does not contain the vulnerable multiply.

Netty 4.1.136.Final causes FIPS test timeout (TestFipsEnd2End hangs on index creation). Investigating compatibility issue with FIPS mode before upgrading. The vulnerability affects DNS codec memory leak with malformed DNS packets, but Elasticsearch's typical deployment does not expose DNS codec to untrusted input.

The fix for GHSA-mhm7-754m-9p8w (jackson-databind 2.18.9 and 2.21.5) is not yet published to Maven Central. Elasticsearch standalone Jackson copies are pinned to 2.18.8 / 2.21.4; parquet-hadoop-bundle 1.17.1 (the latest release) embeds jackson-databind 2.21.3 while awaiting upstream publication of the remaining fix.

DHI forces that bundle over upstream 1.17.0, but no published parquet-hadoop-bundle yet embeds the 2.21.4 fix for GHSA-r7wm-3cxj-wff9. The vulnerability affects async JSON parsing with unbounded number length, but Elasticsearch's typical deployment behind reverse proxies with request size limits provides some mitigation.
